report.summary: Chunk 3 of 5 of cancel.py: defines WindowsJobBackend and PosixSessionBackend classes with methods for process group management on Windows and POSIX.
risks: WindowsJobBackend.signal_group | medium | Uses GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent with CTRL_BREAK_EVENT; may not work for all process groups. | Verify with test: does CTRL_BREAK_EVENT reach all processes in the job?
PosixSessionBackend.signal_group | medium | Uses SIGINT; may not be appropriate for all use cases. | Confirm desired signal behavior.
PosixSessionBackend._pgid | low | Falls back to process.pid on OSError; could mask errors. | Check if fallback is intended.

handoff.purpose: Defines WindowsJobBackend and PosixSessionBackend classes for process group management.

symbols.name: WindowsJobBackend
symbols.note: Uses Windows Job Object to contain process tree; methods: popen_kwargs, before_spawn, after_spawn, signal_group, kill_tree, release.

symbols.name: PosixSessionBackend
symbols.note: Uses POSIX process groups via start_new_session; methods: popen_kwargs, before_spawn, after_spawn, signal_group, kill_tree, release, _pgid.

symbols.name: _resume_all_threads
symbols.note: Not defined in this chunk; used in WindowsJobBackend.after_spawn.

symbols.name: WindowsJobBackend.popen_kwargs
symbols.note: Returns dict with creationflags: CREATE_SUSPENDED | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP.

symbols.name: WindowsJobBackend.before_spawn
symbols.note: Creates a job object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE limit.

symbols.name: WindowsJobBackend.after_spawn
symbols.note: Assigns process to job and resumes all threads via _resume_all_threads.

symbols.name: WindowsJobBackend.kill_tree
symbols.note: Terminates job object with exit code 1; falls back to process.kill() if job is None.

symbols.name: WindowsJobBackend.release
symbols.note: Closes job handle, causing KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE to terminate survivors.

symbols.name: PosixSessionBackend.signal_group
symbols.note: Sends SIGINT to process group via os.killpg.

symbols.name: PosixSessionBackend.kill_tree
symbols.note: Sends SIGKILL to process group via os.killpg; falls back to process.kill() on error.

symbols.name: PosixSessionBackend._pgid
symbols.note: Static method; returns os.getpgid(process.pid) or process.pid on error.

claims.text: Contain the tree in a Job Object that dies with its handle.
claims.why: The class uses KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE flag and closes handle in release(), killing survivors.

claims.text: Contain the tree in its own session/process group.
claims.why: popen_kwargs sets start_new_session=True, creating a new session.

claims.text: Only now is it safe to let the child run: anything it spawns from here on is born inside the job.
claims.why: The comment explains that after AssignProcessToJobObject, child processes are in the job.

claims.text: KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE: closing the last handle destroys any survivor.
claims.why: The comment describes the flag's behavior; the code closes the handle in release().

observations.what: WindowsJobBackend.signal_group uses GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent with CTRL_BREAK_EVENT; may not affect all processes in the job.
PosixSessionBackend.signal_group sends SIGINT; may not be appropriate for all use cases.
PosixSessionBackend._pgid falls back to process.pid on OSError; may mask errors.
WindowsJobBackend.after_spawn uses _resume_all_threads function not defined in this chunk.
WindowsJobBackend.before_spawn uses _JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION and _JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE constants not defined in this chunk.
